samples.claim: Initialize prev_row to 0..=n and curr_row to n+1 zeros. For each s1 char set first current cost i+1; each s2 char has substitution cost0 when equal else1; current[j+1] is min(previous[j+1]+1,current[j]+1,previous[j]+cost), then swap row buffers. Return prev_row[n]. Time is O(m*n) after O(m+n) character collection; two DP rows use O(n), but total auxiliary storage includes both character vectors and is O(m+n). Row width follows s2, not min(m,n). No early cutoff, Result, unsafe code, shared state or IO exists; allocation/arithmetic failures are not caught.
samples.review_note: Matches two-row recurrence and return. Supplemental lines17-29 confirm both character Vec allocations and m/n definitions supporting the total-memory caveat.

Values are Arc<Vec<u8>>. These choices are part of the comparison workload, not exact resident memory.

samples.claim: If the dropped side owns polling, Drop clears polling ownership and takes the waiting peer waker. It releases the mutex before wake(), permitting callbacks that immediately repoll. samples.review_note: Matches clearing polling owner, mutex release before explicit wake and no upstream poll. Supplemental Drop lines82-112 show buffered capacity permits released and comment rationale.

samples.claim: TempObjFile is deliberately different: it owns a temporary directory and caches ObjPath::parse(format!("{}/some_file",tempdir.path_str())).unwrap(). It does not create/open the leaf file; AsRef and Deref borrow the cached ObjPath. The comment explains avoiding an open leaf handle that would prevent atomic renames on Windows. Default retains the directory so the leaf location stays owned, and inherits directory/conversion/parse panic paths.
samples.review_note: Matches owned TempDir, cached object path, no leaf creation, borrow accessors and Windows comment. Supplemental TempDir lines41-89 confirm construction/string conversion panic paths and Default.

samples.claim: fragments_by_offset_range uses logical row offsets, not row IDs: binary_search start in cached N+1 prefix offsets, otherwise insertion index minus1, then walk fragment indices. Break when fragment start>=end OR fragment end<=start; append(start,&Fragment) otherwise. Unknown current length acts as zero. It does not validate/recompute offsets, sort, deduplicate equal offsets or explicitly validate empty/reversed ranges. Duplicated offsets/zero-length fragments may select a zero-length entry and break before later data; callers need valid coherent counts. Returned elements borrow fragments, despite doc return wording showing owned Fragment.
samples.review_note: Matches cached logical-offset binary search and break predicate; zero/unknown length and duplicate-offset concern follow exact control flow without claimed reproduction.

samples.claim: compacted_sstables repeated=9 updates atomically with merge-insert data commits for concurrent-compactor conflict resolution, independently of background shard snapshots. index_catchup repeated=10 records asynchronous base-index rebuild coverage. When catch-up generation trails compaction, indexed readers use SSTable indices for the gap. Missing index progress keeps needed SSTables live until repair. Only the dedicated WAL repair path adds progress; ordinary index-changing operations remove entries because they cannot attest coverage.

DataOverlay.groups=1 attaches sparse cell changes without rewriting base files. samples.claim: hash_to_block_index takes high32 bits of hash, saturating-multiplies by number of blocks in u64, then shifts right32 and casts usize. For ordinary positive block counts this maps the upper hash fraction to a block; extremely large counts with saturation bias mapping. insert<T:AsBytes+?Sized> and check hash canonical bytes through hash_as_bytes; insert_hash/check_hash use low32 for the block mask and directly index. Empty raw filters panic. check_hash docs simultaneously allow false positives and claim every uninserted hash returns false; the latter is incorrect for a Bloom filter and contradicted by the bit-test algorithm. Correct guarantee for matching hash/layout is no false negatives for inserted hashes; false means definitely absent.
samples.review_note: Matches high32 saturating block mapping, byte-hash delegation, direct indexing and contradictory false-positive doc. Supplemental Block lines98-151 confirms OR/all-mask-bit membership reasoning.
